name: supercell_333m
description: The Phase 3 supercell: a classic Weisman-Klemp splitting supercell at 333 m, in a Bunkers-tracked moving domain. This is the first SHEARED, MOVING, ASYMMETRIC scenario in the project. Physically it is the Phase 0 validation storm (canonical WK supercell -- deep sustained updraft, split into counter-rotating left/right movers, peak w 60.6 m/s @ 83 min) promoted to the production microphysics (NSSL ptype=27) and the 333 m overnight tier. As the deck-generator advisor guessed and the plan (docs/phase3-plan-2026-07-20.md 2.2) confirmed, the base template IS that validation deck, so this scenario mostly STOPS overriding it: single_cell drove iwnd->0 and imove->0 to get a zero-shear pulse cell; the supercell keeps the template's iwnd=2 shear and imove=1 moving frame. Its asymmetric, splitting storm is what discharges the Phase 2 T9 cref orientation test (plan 2.4).

namelist._note: Deltas FROM single_cell_333m (which is the zero-shear baseline): iwnd 0->2 (WK unidirectional shear), imove 0->1 (Bunkers moving frame) with umove/vmove now REQUIRED and non-zero, and the domain grows to 360x360 to hold the split. ptype=27 and the vertical grid are unchanged from the baseline. Every REQUIRED_KEY is declared explicitly (deck.py does NOT default them) even where the value matches the template -- that is the design: generating the scenario must exercise every override, never silently inherit.
namelist._domain_note: 540 x 333 m = 179.82 km (half-width 89.91 km). ENLARGED from the Phase 0 120 km grid after the FIRST T1 run (360x360, 2026-07-21) empirically resolved watch-item 1: the Phase 0 flat/imove containment (120 km held the split with 26 km clearance) was measured at 1 km/Morrison, and it does NOT hold at 333 m/NSSL. The finer grid + true-hail microphysics grew a more expansive storm: anvil filled the 120 km domain from t~65 min (benign -- open/radiative BCs, wbc..nbc=2, so it advects out, not wraparound), but REAL low-level convection (|w| up to 17 m/s and a 47 dBZ precip core at z=3-6 km, NOT damping-layer noise) reached the +y/-x open boundary in the final ~12 min (t>=108 min). The primary left/right mover updraft cores (+55/-50 m/s) stayed mid-level and interior throughout, and the split itself was textbook (left mover NW-drifting, right mover near-centre, Bunkers umove/vmove verified good) -- so the physics was sound and only the DOMAIN was marginal. Owner call (2026-07-21): re-run larger rather than accept-with-caveat or truncate. 540 gives ~15-20 km clearance to the fast-growing +y convection edge (which reached ~60 km clipped and was still advancing ~1.3 km/min). Cost ~2.25x the 360 run (~420 GB raw, within the 1024 GB VHDX; ~4.5 h wall-clock at np=8). The bubble stays domain-centred (iorigin=2), so the split reproduces identically with room to spare. Vertical grid unchanged (nz=40, dz=500, ztop 19.75 km).
namelist._timing_note: 2 h storm (timax=7200), matching the Phase 0 validation window in which the split fully develops (2 cores separated by 75 min, 46 km apart by 120 min). tapfrq=12 s -> 601 output frames, the same 12 s cadence as single_cell (owner's choice for dense playback); heavier raw I/O than 301 frames but well within the VHDX budget. dtl=2.0 s is the CFL-limited 333 m step (docs/phase0-benchmark.md 4); adapt_dt=1 adapts from there.
namelist._rstfrq_note: OPTIONAL run-control override (deck.py Category 5), NOT part of the scenario identity. Hourly restart files (rstfrq=3600 s). The template default is -3600 (restarts OFF), verified: the first 360-run wrote no rst*.nc. This enlarged run is ~4.5 h -- past the charter's 'restarts safely skippable only on short 2-3 h runs' line -- so a mid-run crash costs time, not a full re-run. restart_reset_frqtim=.true. and restart_filetype=2 (netCDF) come from the template &param16.
namelist._seed_note: UNSEEDED. Phase 3 T4 made `seed` a REQUIRED key, emitted as CM1's var7 (sim/cm1-patches/README.md). This scenario runs irandp=0 -- no random perturbations at all -- so it has no stochastic component to seed, and seed=0 declares that explicitly rather than leaving it to a default. deck.py REFUSES a positive seed at irandp=0: the seed advance lives inside `IF( irandp.eq.1 )THEN`, so it would be read, broadcast and silently ignored. seed=0 substitutes 0.0 into a template line that already reads 0.0, so this scenario's generated deck is byte-identical to its pre-T4 deck -- verified, docs/phase3-t4-seed.md.
namelist._storm_note: isnd=5 WK analytic sounding; iwnd=2 the WK unidirectional shear profile that makes a supercell (the single defining change from the pulse cell); iinit=1 single warm bubble (irandp=0 -- so two diverging cores can ONLY be a split, not independent cells, exactly as Phase 0 argued); icor=0 (the canonical WK case runs Coriolis-off); imove=1 Bunkers moving frame; iorigin=2 centred coordinates. Output x/y are in the MOVING frame, so the domain stays centred at (0,0) and the symmetric-about-origin export box (the only mode the pipeline supports) is exactly right: the right mover sits near (0,0), the left mover's NW drift becomes the box's asymmetric bulge, and the box CENTRE stays static at (0,0) -- the SVT constraint, satisfied for free.
namelist._motion_note: Bunkers right-mover storm-motion estimate, inherited from the Phase 0 validation deck (docs/phase0-validation.md). REQUIRED (not derivable) whenever imove=1 -- deck.py refuses imove=1 without them. This scenario is the FIRST positive exercise of the imove=1 branch in the deck generator; it was previously reached only by negative controls (Phase 2 10.4).
namelist._micro_note: NSSL 2-moment, ptype=27 (true hail category) -- the production microphysics, unchanged from single_cell. The Phase 0 supercell was validated with Morrison (ptype=5); this is the FIRST NSSL supercell, so the split's development is eyeballed in the output (plan 3, watch-item 3; formally checked in T2).

provenance.namelist: GENERATED by pipeline/gen_deck.py from this file -- no hand-written deck exists for this scenario.
provenance.shear: WK unidirectional shear (iwnd=2) -- the supercell-producing profile, validated in Phase 0
provenance.initiation: single warm bubble (iinit=1), no random perturbations (irandp=0)

export._note: MEASURED box -- from the ENLARGED (540) run's OWN active-voxel union, `export_scenario.py bbox` over all 601 frames (2026-07-21). The crop box is an OUTPUT of the run, not an input (Phase 1 learned the expensive way that a box copied from elsewhere clips the real storm and exports anyway). Union: horizontal half-width 89.744 km == the FULL domain half-width, condensate top 17.750 km, peak-active frame 600 (1.95M CM1 voxels). The box below CONTAINS that union at clean 333 m voxel counts: 540x540x54 (the horizontal grid is the native sim grid 1:1, no crop and no resample -- the anvil fills the domain, so there is nothing smaller to crop to). This storm is ASYMMETRIC (splitting + NW-drifting left mover) and the box reaches BOTH movers with room, which is what lets it discharge the T3/T9 cref orientation test.
export._voxel_note: NATIVE 333 m -- the sim grid, no resampling (same rule as single_cell_333m: the export voxel tracks the simulation resolution). At 540x540x54 the export grid CENTRES coincide with the CM1 grid centres 1:1 horizontally (nx_export=540=nx_sim), so the horizontal crop is a pass-through; only the vertical is an upsample of the 500 m CM1 levels to 333 m, as in single_cell_333m.
export._half_width_note: MEASURED. 89910 m -> nx = 2*89910/333 = 540 = the full native grid. The measured active-voxel union half-width came back at 89.744 km == the outermost CM1 cell centre, i.e. the ANVIL FILLS THE DOMAIN: condensate first touches the wall at frame 436 (t=87 min) and reaches +89.7 km thereafter. That is benign -- open/radiative BCs (wbc..nbc=2), so it is cirrus advecting OUT, not wraparound -- but it means the honest horizontal box IS the whole domain (89744 itself is not an integer voxel count, so the box is set to the full grid, 89910, which contains the union with +166 m margin). CAVEAT accepted: a domain-sized box necessarily carries thin far-field anvil out to the boundary; fine this phase (web-only, no SVT static-bbox penalty). active_mask does NOT include w (signed, web-only); the exporter checks the w extent separately. CONTAINMENT (probe_edge.py, the T1 acceptance gate): dbz>=40 CORE never touches the wall (~40 km clearance), and the main |w|>=10 updraft body holds ~40-45 km clearance steady through t=108-117 min -- the decisive improvement over the 360 run, whose sustained convection sat AT the wall. The one marginal number, +65.8 km |w|>=10 (23.5 km clearance), is a single 23-voxel, 11.9 m/s flanking cell at z=4.5 km that appears ONLY at the terminal frame (t=120 min = timax), 21 km downshear of the main body -- real physics but a footnote, with no un-simulated future in which it reaches the wall. Advisor concurred: PASS, not marginal.
export._z_top_note: MEASURED. 17982 m -> nz = 17982/333 = 54, containing the measured CONDENSATE top of 17.750 km (the provisional nz=53/17649 m clipped it by 101 m). Set from the condensate top, NOT the |w| top: |w|>=10 reached ~18.25 km late in the run, but that upper-level w sits in the zd=15 km Rayleigh damping layer (numerical, not clean updraft), so it is not an honest export ceiling. probe_wsurge.py confirmed the far/high w is damping-layer or terminal-flank, not a deep convective tower needing more lid.
